title: Launcher action, in line: a pusher between two curved arms shaped by the beam solver, a flooded frame, the disc flat in a roofed slot, the stem trapped in a guide, a hooked sear on one flexure and a trigger blade, printed in one piece on its side

findings.text: the frame is flooded: 4210 mm² solid, all but the room the moving parts sweep (17 loose bits left out)
hole 1 (⌀4.1 at -105.2, 32) is in solid frame, 3 mm of wall round it
hole 2 (⌀4.1 at -105.2, -32) is in solid frame, 3 mm of wall round it
hole 3 (⌀4.1 at 49.3, 32) is in solid frame, 3 mm of wall round it
hole 4 (⌀4.1 at 49.3, -32) is in solid frame, 3 mm of wall round it
everything clears what it isn't joined to by 0.3 mm, and each flexure touches only its two bodies: it prints free
rest to drawn: clear all the way
drawn to cocked: settles on sear at 10.79 mm (spring)
cocked to pulled: clear all the way
pulled to fired: clear all the way
fired to rest: clear all the way
drawn: nothing runs into anything
cocked: nothing runs into anything (hinge pushed 0.66° by what it meets)
pulled: nothing runs into anything
fired: nothing runs into anything
cocked: nothing holds pusher: pushed 1.08 back towards rest it passes sear, pushing it aside: it would take a friction over 0.11 to hold (checked at 0.1); tilt the catch so the load presses it in
spring: 1.26 mm thick: 3 lines of 0.42 mm
spring: 10.56 mm wide is 52.80 layers of 0.2 mm: a whole number prints as drawn
spring: at its most (11.2 mm) it sees 0.93% strain, within the limit of 1.25% (14.92 mm)
spring: finite elements give a peak of 1.12% at (-29.5, 30.2) (1.20 × beam theory), within the limit of 1.25%
spring: stopped by the ground at 11.85 mm, before its limit of 12.48 mm (by its finite-element peak)
hinge: 1.81 mm thick is 4.31 lines of 0.42 mm: a whole number prints as drawn (1.68 mm)
hinge: 10.56 mm wide is 52.80 layers of 0.2 mm: a whole number prints as drawn
hinge: at its most (7°) it sees 0.81% strain, within the limit of 1.25% (7.17°)
hinge: finite elements give a peak of 0.01% at (-74.3, 15.1) (0.02 × beam theory), within the limit of 1.25%
hinge: nothing stops it before 7.17°, where it breaks: add a hard stop (a post or a wall it meets)
the most stored is 0.045 J, in pulled; at their most: spring 7.67 N at 11.2 mm, hinge 89.8 N·mm at 7°
rest to drawn: driving spring 11.19 mm takes up to 8.41 N
cocked: let go of, pusher stays on sear, 10.64 mm from rest, which takes 7.4 N (beams and contact, friction 0.3)
cocked to pulled: driving hinge 1.87 mm takes up to 8.99 N
cocked to pulled: pusher is let go 79% of the way, with hinge moved 1.4 mm under 6.47 N, and jumps 10.4 mm
back at rest, everything is where it started
cocked to pulled: pulling hinge 1.4 mm, at up to 6.47 N, lets pusher go: the catch held 7.4 N, 0.87 of it on the finger (friction 0.3)
fired from pulled (from the moment the trigger lets go): pusher reaches 2.0 m/s; disc leaves at 2.0 m/s after 6.4 ms, with 1.7 mJ: 4% of the 43.1 mJ stored, within the 80 mJ allowed
spring: bending as far as it bends through the sequence, it sees up to 0.93% strain (large-deflection beams), within the limit of 1.25%
hinge: bending as far as it bends through the sequence, it sees up to 1.25% strain (large-deflection beams), within the limit of 1.25%
bridge 1 spans no more than the 22 mm the printer bridges
bridge 1 stands on the frame on both sides
guide 1: pusher runs in it for 35.2 mm with a 1.50 mm ridge in a groove, flanks at 45°: held across the plane
guide 2: sear runs in it for 11.3 mm with a 1.50 mm ridge in a groove, flanks at 45°: held across the plane
the frame bends up to 0.06 mm under the flexures' pull; at drawn it closes 0.02 mm towards disc, leaving 0.38 mm
pusher: pushed 1.0 N across the plane at (-91.0, 0.0) (a tenth of the hand's pull), it moves 0.00 mm out of the plane
sear: pushed 1.0 N across the plane at (-75.0, 32.0) (a tenth of the hand's pull), it moves 0.00 mm out of the plane
